newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's considers legal action against U.S. Names.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's considers legal action against U.S. Names.

text.p: Lloyd's of London insurance market is considering taking legal action against investors in the United States who have not accepted its 3.2 billion stg settlement package, a Lloyd's spokesman said on Monday.
But the insurance market may wait until November before issuing writs against U.S. investors, or Names, who did not sign up for the offer, which was accepted by many Names in August.

Last week, Lloyd's issued 200 writs in the English High Court against some of the 1,800 Names who had not accepted the compensation deal for losses incurred in recent years. It is looking to recover some 500 million stg from these Names.
More than 32,000 Names have signed up for the settlement package and, in return, agreed to end legal action against Lloyd's and its agents.

In the United States, where litigation against Lloyd's has been intense, the insurance market's efforts to secure its future culminated in a deal ending action by state regulators in return for Lloyd's giving extra financial assistance to Names.
A last-ditch attempt in late August by one group of Names to derail the insurance market's recovery plan failed after Lloyd's successfully appealed a debilitating court ruling.
But the United States still poses some degree of complexity, not least in enforceability. Lloyd's could have issued writs against U.S. Names this week, but may not do so until November.
The next batch of writs is due to go out later this month and Names resident in Canada might be included among these.
There are some 660 North American Names in all who have not accepted the settlement offer, who together could owe the insurance market an estimated 170 million stg.
